# 003 — Draw each post's feature image in the browser from a fixed template

**Decision** — The feature image for each post is a branded title card that the blog page draws itself, in the site's colors and fonts, and offers as a PNG download.

**Why this came up** — Every LinkedIn post needs an image, and images get noticed in the feed. The image either had to be generated by an AI image model or drawn from a template.

**Options**
- **Branded title card drawn by code** — theme title, date and the five project names, in the site's Cobalt style. Cost: less eye-catching than an illustration; a shared blog link won't show the card as its preview.
- **AI illustration per post** — an image model draws a scene for each theme. Cost: about $0.04 to $0.25 per image, a place to store images, and AI art that can look generic to LinkedIn readers.
- **AI art with the title on top** — both. Cost: the most moving parts and the highest cost.

**What we chose and why** — The title card. Tarik chose it from the three options; it was Claude's recommendation. It costs nothing to make, needs no storage, and looks the same every day, so followers can recognize the series in their feed. Drawing it in the browser means no server code for images at all.

**What we gave up** — Visual variety, and a link preview image for the blog page itself.

**How we'll know if this was right** — After four weeks of posts, compare engagement on these posts with Tarik's other image posts. Tarik makes that comparison.
